GenZSalud: I Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Liderazgo de Jóvenes Investigadores en Ciencias de la Salud
events.description:
La Universidad de Málaga acoge GenZSalud, el I Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Liderazgo de Jóvenes Investigadores en Ciencias de la Salud. Su objetivo es impulsar el talento emergente, promover la cultura investigadora y favorecer la transferencia de conocimiento con impacto social.

GenZSalud ofrece un espacio internacional en el que jóvenes investigadores —desde estudiantes de Grado y Máster hasta doctorandos y personal investigador en etapas iniciales o consolidadas— pueden presentar sus proyectos, fortalecer competencias profesionales y crear redes de colaboración transdisciplinar.

El congreso actúa como plataforma estratégica para difundir el potencial de la investigación joven, conectar con el sector sanitario, la industria y la sociedad, y fomentar la internacionalización mediante sinergias con instituciones y redes de alcance global. Además, potencia habilidades clave en comunicación científica, pensamiento crítico y liderazgo investigador.

La celebración de GenZSalud reafirma el compromiso de la Universidad de Málaga con la formación de talento joven y la consolidación de ecosistemas científicos dinámicos y competitivos. Contribuye a intensificar la proyección internacional de la UMA, visibilizar sus líneas de investigación y fortalecer la conexión entre universidad, sistema sanitario y ciudadanía.

En definitiva, GenZSalud es un espacio formativo de excelencia que impulsa la innovación en Ciencias de la Salud, promueve la cooperación internacional y sitúa a los jóvenes investigadores en el centro del liderazgo científico.

El programa abordará tres bloques temáticos:

  • Innovación y tecnologías emergentes:

           - Inteligencia artificial y análisis de datos en salud.

           - Nuevas herramientas y dispositivos biomédicos.

           - Soluciones digitales para el cuidado y la prevención.

  • Investigación clínica y salud pública:

          - Nuevos enfoques en diagnóstico y tratamiento.

          - Estrategias para la promoción de la salud y la prevención de enfermedades.

         - Impacto de la investigación en politicas de salud.

  • Liderazgo, emprendimiento, divulgación y transferencia:

         - Comunicación científica y divulgación de la investigación.

         - Desarrollo de habilidades de liderazgo en jóvenes investigadores.

         - Construcción de redes y colaboración internacional.

         - Creación de proyectos de emprendimiento.

         - Transferencia universidad - industria.

events.name: BIP Ethical Hacking: Build Cybersecurity Skills with Kauno Kolegija
events.description:
This Blended Intensive Programme (BIP) is designed to equip students with practical skills in ethical hacking, with a strong focus on network security and artificial intelligence (AI) security. Participants will explore how attacks on AI systems work, conduct penetration testing, carry out vulnerability assessments, and learn to set up and use Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS).

The programme also covers packet analysis using Wireshark, a wide range of cybersecurity tools, and effective defense strategies — giving participants both theoretical grounding and real-world experience through hands-on simulations and team-based challenges.


Check spot availability and register your institution's interest by reaching out directly to the programme coordinator at Kauno Kolegija: Rita Kmitė — rita.kmite@go.kauko.lt

events.name: BIP: SHAPING THE FUTURE OF HEALTH: YOUNG RESEARCHERS LEADING CHANGE
events.description:
Join us for this Blended Intensive Programme about young researchers in health

The main objective of this Blended Intensive Program is to empower young people in the field of health sciences by providing them with the skills, tools, and international perspective needed to lead innovation and positive change in the health sector. Furthermore, this program aims to foster multi-perspective collaborations, enhance scientific skills, and promote active engagement in assessing emerging global health challenges.


The BIP has been designed to include students from different European institutions to work collaboratively during several months on real-world problems. To achieve this purpose, this program combine a previous online preparation, intensive face-to-face activities, and a follow-up period. During this period, participants will engage in project-based learning, hands-on workshops, cultural activities, visits to the Spanish healthcare system, debates and expert-led seminars focused on innovation, digital health, new research trends, scientific communication, leadership, and clinical research.


The virtual component will be focused on preparation, team formation and basic knowledge acquisition to enable students to manage themselves in the face-to-face activities with a well-founded knowledge.


The face-to-face activities will be focused on interaction with professional and researchers from several countries, allowing students to be involved in an international congress of young researchers, cultural activities and real-work environment in the host institution.


The follow-up will be online, and the participants will present their projects and receive feedback from an international panel of experts.


Overall, this BIP seeks to promote international collaboration, strengthen scientific and professional abilities and inspire young people to become leaders of the change in the health field across Europe.

events.name: Erasmus+ BIP: Culture, Languages and Responsible Tourism
events.description:
The BIP "Culture, Languages and Responsible and Sustainable Tourism" is an innovative mobility programme co-organised with the University Sorbonne Paris Nord and the University of Malaga. It is open to students from UNINOVIS member universities and is designed to build intercultural, analytical, and professional skills in the field of responsible tourism and heritage management.

The programme focuses on semi-peripheral destinations, such as the Caserta area north-east of Naples, where cultural heritage and sustainable tourism meet real community needs. Students will engage directly with local actors, social cooperatives, and heritage sites.

Why it matters: sustainable tourism requires professionals who can connect cultural heritage with social and ethical responsibility. This BIP offers students direct exposure to real communities, local tourism operators, and internationally recognised academics working at that intersection.


Registration requirements


All students wishing to participate must meet the following requirements at the time of nomination:

  • Eligible degree: bachelor's or master's students in languages, history, cultural mediation, economics, or tourism sociology.
  • English proficiency: minimum B1 level required.
  • University affiliation: nominations must be submitted through your UNINOVIS member university.

Nominations close May 20. Each partner university may nominate up to 5 students.


For further information, please contact the academic coordinator Prof. Olivier Butzbach at olivierkarl.butzbach@unicampania.it or reach out through the UNINOVIS Alliance network.

events.name: The UNINOVIS Hackathon "Resilient AI-Powered Supply Chain"
events.description:
The UNINOVIS Hackathon "Resilient AI-Powered Supply Chain" is an international, interdisciplinary hackathon where students develop innovative solutions to enhance the resilience of logistics and supply chains. During the event, teams will tackle real-world challenges related to artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, transportation and warehousing processes, and risk management. 

Main Theme: 

Resilient AI-Powered Supply Chain – exploring how generative artificial intelligence and cybersecurity principles can be used to create safer, more resilient, and more efficient logistics and supply chains.


The hackathon will take place on 17–19 November 2026, and students who successfully complete the programme will receive 3 ECTS credits.


1. Objectives

1.      To provide students with opportunities to apply their knowledge of artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, and logistics in practice;

2.      To foster innovation, creativity, teamwork, and problem-solving skills;

3.      To develop prototypes of new products, services, and processes that improve supply chain resilience;

4.      To strengthen the international identity of UNINOVIS and collaboration with industry partners;

5.      To develop future-oriented competencies in artificial intelligence and cybersecurity.


The hackathon is primarily intended for students of Logistics, Transport Logistics, Management, Business Analytics, Business Informatics, Information Systems, Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Economics, and Industrial Engineering. However, participation is open to all students interested in artificial intelligence, digitalization, innovation, and supply chain resilience.

events.name: Virtual Workshop: Innovative Teaching Practices in the Age of AI
events.description:
Submit your proposal here:

Virtual Workshop: Innovative Teaching Practices in the Age of AI  

      

Context

Artificial intelligence is rapidly transforming higher education. Students now have access to tools that can generate essays, solve problems, write code, and summarise literature. This shift challenges us to rethink what we teach, how we teach, and how we assess learning.

Across UNINOVIS, many teachers are already responding to these challenges with creative and effective approaches. This call aims to identify, document, and share these innovations across the alliance.

Who is this call for?

Any teacher, lecturer, or instructor at a UNINOVIS partner institution who has adapted their teaching practice in response to the challenges or opportunities created by AI. We are looking for practitioners at any level — from small adjustments in a single course to comprehensive programme redesigns.

What we are looking for

We want to hear about pedagogical innovations that address one or more of the following goals:

A. Fostering active student participation — strategies that shift students from passive consumers to active contributors in the learning process

B. Developing critical thinking — approaches that train students to question, evaluate, and reason independently, including evaluating AI-generated content

C. Authentic assessment — moving beyond traditional exams toward assessments that reflect real-world competences and are resilient to AI misuse

D. Learning by doing — hands-on, experiential approaches where students learn through practice and application

E. Personalised learning — adapting the learning experience to individual student needs, pace, or interests

F. Interdisciplinary and collaborative learning — breaking disciplinary silos and building teamwork skills across fields, institutions, or countries

G. Ethical awareness and social responsibility — embedding reflection on the societal impact of AI and professional practice

H. Creativity and original production — encouraging students to produce genuinely original work that goes beyond what AI can generate

How do you innovate?

We are also interested in understanding how you innovate. Your approach may involve one or more of the following strategies:

  1. Redesigning the learning activity — changing what happens in the classroom (new dynamics, formats, or interactions). This may involve changing the role of the student (increasing student responsibility, autonomy, or agency), changing the role of the teacher (redefining the teacher’s function from knowledge transmitter to facilitator, mentor, or coach)
  2. Designing tasks that promote creativity and critical thinking — a deep understanding of written text
  3. Redesigning assessment — changing how student learning is evaluated
  4. Cross-boundary collaboration — innovating through collaboration across disciplines, institutions, or countries
  5. Other approaches

What to submit

Click the link to submission and answer the questions prompted in the Google Forms, it will ask for a short description (maximum 500 words) covering:

  1. Your context
    1. Institution
    2. Scientific domain (Arts, Humanities, Social Sciences, Sciences, Computer Science, other engineering specialities, etc.)
    3. Course title or short description
    4. Level (bachelor/master) and approximate class size
    5. (Optional) Any other relevant information
  2. The challenge — what problem or opportunity prompted you to change your practice
  3. Your innovation — what you did differently and how it works in practice
  4. Pedagogical goals — which of the goals above (A–H) your innovation addresses
  5. Innovation strategy — which of the strategies above (1–4) best describes your approach
  6. Results or observations — what impact you have observed, even if informal or anecdotal
  7. (Optional) Link to resources — a link to a web page, platform, or material you use with your students that illustrates your approach

Submissions do not need to be polished academic papers. We value practical experience and honest reflection over formal research methodology. 

What happens next

The selection process will seek to ensure representation across different disciplines, so that the resulting compendium and workshop reflect the breadth of teaching contexts within the alliance.

Selected contributions will be:

  • Featured in a UNINOVIS compendium of innovative teaching practices shared across all partner institutions
  • Invited to make a presentation (10 minutes + 2 minutes for questions) of their proposal at UNINOVIS Virtual Workshop Innovative Teaching Practices in the Age of AI. Note that time constraints may force the organisers to limit the number of invitations.
  • Considered for participation in an in-person workshop during the spring of 2027

Committees

The scientific committee will evaluate proposals and select the ones that will go forward.

Confirmed members of the scientific committee

  • Zeynep Azar (Haagse Hogeschool, Netherlands)
  • Fjoralba Dado (Universiteti i Tiranës, Albania)
  • Claudia Diers-Lienke (Haagse Hogeschool, Netherlands)
  • Clotilde Lechuga (Universidad de Málaga, Spain)
  • Eleonore Lemmerich (Technische Hochschule Würzburg-Schweinfurt, Germany)
  • Jeffrey Michael Taylor (Kauno Kolegija, Lithuania)
  • Irene Moreno Medina (Universidad de Málaga, Spain)
  • Ignacio Moreno-Torres (Universidad de Málaga, Spain)
  • Marijana Prodanovic (Kauno Kolegija, Lithuania)
  • Ligita Zailskaitė-Jakštė (Kauno Kolegija, Lithuania)
  • Amparo Zamora (Universidad de Málaga, Spain)

Members of the organising committee

  • Francisca Martín Vergara (Universidad de Málaga)
  • Ignacio Moreno-Torres Sánchez (Universidad de Málaga)
  • Marijana Prodanovic (Kauno Kolegija) 
  • Yamina Seamari (Universidad de Málaga)
  • Amparo Zamora Mogollo (Universidad de Málaga)

catalogue_events.x_programme:
Skills and competencies

The programme is built around learning by doing. Through a mix of lectures, hands-on labs, and team-based challenges, participants will develop a solid foundation in both offensive and defensive cybersecurity — as well as the soft skills needed to work effectively in multidisciplinary teams. By the end of the programme, students will have developed competencies in:

  • Ethical hacking principles and teamwork in a cybersecurity context
  • Communication and presentation of technical findings
  • Working in simulation environments to practise cybersecurity scenarios
  • Practical packet analysis using Wireshark
  • Cybersecurity attack methods and the tools used to carry them out
  • Penetration testing and Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS)
  • Understanding and defending against attacks on AI systems

Beyond the technical content, the programme aims to build participants' confidence and adaptability — equipping them with the mindset and tools needed to keep learning as the cybersecurity landscape continues to evolve.

catalogue_events.name: Erasmus+ BIP: Culture, Languages and Responsible Tourism
catalogue_events.description:
The BIP "Culture, Languages and Responsible and Sustainable Tourism" is an innovative mobility programme co-organised with the University Sorbonne Paris Nord and the University of Malaga. It is open to students from UNINOVIS member universities and is designed to build intercultural, analytical, and professional skills in the field of responsible tourism and heritage management.

The programme focuses on semi-peripheral destinations, such as the Caserta area north-east of Naples, where cultural heritage and sustainable tourism meet real community needs. Students will engage directly with local actors, social cooperatives, and heritage sites.

Why it matters: sustainable tourism requires professionals who can connect cultural heritage with social and ethical responsibility. This BIP offers students direct exposure to real communities, local tourism operators, and internationally recognised academics working at that intersection.


Registration requirements


All students wishing to participate must meet the following requirements at the time of nomination:

  • Eligible degree: bachelor's or master's students in languages, history, cultural mediation, economics, or tourism sociology.
  • English proficiency: minimum B1 level required.
  • University affiliation: nominations must be submitted through your UNINOVIS member university.

Nominations close May 20. Each partner university may nominate up to 5 students.


For further information, please contact the academic coordinator Prof. Olivier Butzbach at olivierkarl.butzbach@unicampania.it or reach out through the UNINOVIS Alliance network.

catalogue_events.name: GenZSalud: I Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Liderazgo de Jóvenes Investigadores en Ciencias de la Salud
catalogue_events.description:
La Universidad de Málaga acoge GenZSalud, el I Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Liderazgo de Jóvenes Investigadores en Ciencias de la Salud. Su objetivo es impulsar el talento emergente, promover la cultura investigadora y favorecer la transferencia de conocimiento con impacto social.

GenZSalud ofrece un espacio internacional en el que jóvenes investigadores —desde estudiantes de Grado y Máster hasta doctorandos y personal investigador en etapas iniciales o consolidadas— pueden presentar sus proyectos, fortalecer competencias profesionales y crear redes de colaboración transdisciplinar.

El congreso actúa como plataforma estratégica para difundir el potencial de la investigación joven, conectar con el sector sanitario, la industria y la sociedad, y fomentar la internacionalización mediante sinergias con instituciones y redes de alcance global. Además, potencia habilidades clave en comunicación científica, pensamiento crítico y liderazgo investigador.

La celebración de GenZSalud reafirma el compromiso de la Universidad de Málaga con la formación de talento joven y la consolidación de ecosistemas científicos dinámicos y competitivos. Contribuye a intensificar la proyección internacional de la UMA, visibilizar sus líneas de investigación y fortalecer la conexión entre universidad, sistema sanitario y ciudadanía.

En definitiva, GenZSalud es un espacio formativo de excelencia que impulsa la innovación en Ciencias de la Salud, promueve la cooperación internacional y sitúa a los jóvenes investigadores en el centro del liderazgo científico.

El programa abordará tres bloques temáticos:

  • Innovación y tecnologías emergentes:

           - Inteligencia artificial y análisis de datos en salud.

           - Nuevas herramientas y dispositivos biomédicos.

           - Soluciones digitales para el cuidado y la prevención.

  • Investigación clínica y salud pública:

          - Nuevos enfoques en diagnóstico y tratamiento.

          - Estrategias para la promoción de la salud y la prevención de enfermedades.

         - Impacto de la investigación en politicas de salud.

  • Liderazgo, emprendimiento, divulgación y transferencia:

         - Comunicación científica y divulgación de la investigación.

         - Desarrollo de habilidades de liderazgo en jóvenes investigadores.

         - Construcción de redes y colaboración internacional.

         - Creación de proyectos de emprendimiento.

         - Transferencia universidad - industria.

catalogue_events.name: The UNINOVIS Hackathon "Resilient AI-Powered Supply Chain"
catalogue_events.description:
The UNINOVIS Hackathon "Resilient AI-Powered Supply Chain" is an international, interdisciplinary hackathon where students develop innovative solutions to enhance the resilience of logistics and supply chains. During the event, teams will tackle real-world challenges related to artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, transportation and warehousing processes, and risk management. 

Main Theme: 

Resilient AI-Powered Supply Chain – exploring how generative artificial intelligence and cybersecurity principles can be used to create safer, more resilient, and more efficient logistics and supply chains.


The hackathon will take place on 17–19 November 2026, and students who successfully complete the programme will receive 3 ECTS credits.


1. Objectives

1.      To provide students with opportunities to apply their knowledge of artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, and logistics in practice;

2.      To foster innovation, creativity, teamwork, and problem-solving skills;

3.      To develop prototypes of new products, services, and processes that improve supply chain resilience;

4.      To strengthen the international identity of UNINOVIS and collaboration with industry partners;

5.      To develop future-oriented competencies in artificial intelligence and cybersecurity.


The hackathon is primarily intended for students of Logistics, Transport Logistics, Management, Business Analytics, Business Informatics, Information Systems, Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Economics, and Industrial Engineering. However, participation is open to all students interested in artificial intelligence, digitalization, innovation, and supply chain resilience.

catalogue_events.name: Virtual Workshop: Innovative Teaching Practices in the Age of AI
catalogue_events.description:
Submit your proposal here:

Submit proposal for Virtual Workshop: Innovative Teaching Practices in the Age of AI

Registration is now open:

Register here for the workshop (only for those not presenting!) ​                               ​ ​ ​  ​



News

  • A study with Chinese students in grades 7-12 (Strongber, Ley & Wu, 2026) finds that AI adoption raises homework scores by 18% and reduces completion time by 30%, but lowers monthly exam scores by 20% within six months.
  • We are glad to announce that Dr. Marc-Oliver Gewaltig will give a keynote presentation entitled Writing with AI: Principles, Disclosure and Practical Strategies. Dr. Gewaltig's extensive experience as a neuroscience researcher, as well as his involvement in the development of tools that encourage responsible AI use (see thesify.ai), will surely inspire many of the attendees at the ITP Workshop. Have you not heard about Dr. Gewaltig? You may want to watch this very interesting interview.


Context

Artificial intelligence is rapidly transforming higher education. Students now have access to tools that can generate essays, solve problems, write code, and summarise literature. This shift challenges us to rethink what we teach, how we teach, and how we assess learning.

Across UNINOVIS, many teachers are already responding to these challenges with creative and effective approaches. This call aims to identify, document, and share these innovations across the alliance.

Who is this call for?

Any teacher, lecturer, or instructor at a UNINOVIS partner institution who has adapted their teaching practice in response to the challenges or opportunities created by AI. We are looking for practitioners at any level — from small adjustments in a single course to comprehensive programme redesigns.

What we are looking for

We want to hear about pedagogical innovations that address one or more of the following goals:

A. Fostering active student participation — strategies that shift students from passive consumers to active contributors in the learning process

B. Developing critical thinking — approaches that train students to question, evaluate, and reason independently, including evaluating AI-generated content

C. Authentic assessment — moving beyond traditional exams toward assessments that reflect real-world competences and are resilient to AI misuse

D. Learning by doing — hands-on, experiential approaches where students learn through practice and application

E. Personalised learning — adapting the learning experience to individual student needs, pace, or interests

F. Interdisciplinary and collaborative learning — breaking disciplinary silos and building teamwork skills across fields, institutions, or countries

G. Ethical awareness and social responsibility — embedding reflection on the societal impact of AI and professional practice

H. Creativity and original production — encouraging students to produce genuinely original work that goes beyond what AI can generate

How do you innovate?

We are also interested in understanding how you innovate. Your approach may involve one or more of the following strategies:

  1. Redesigning the learning activity — changing what happens in the classroom (new dynamics, formats, or interactions). This may involve changing the role of the student (increasing student responsibility, autonomy, or agency), changing the role of the teacher (redefining the teacher’s function from knowledge transmitter to facilitator, mentor, or coach)
  2. Designing tasks that promote creativity and critical thinking — a deep understanding of written text
  3. Redesigning assessment — changing how student learning is evaluated
  4. Cross-boundary collaboration — innovating through collaboration across disciplines, institutions, or countries
  5. Other approaches

What to submit

Click the link to submission and answer the questions prompted in the Google Forms, it will ask for a short description (maximum 500 words) covering:

  1. Your context
    1. Institution
    2. Scientific domain (Arts, Humanities, Social Sciences, Sciences, Computer Science, other engineering specialities, etc.)
    3. Course title or short description
    4. Level (bachelor/master) and approximate class size
    5. (Optional) Any other relevant information
  2. The challenge — what problem or opportunity prompted you to change your practice
  3. Your innovation — what you did differently and how it works in practice
  4. Pedagogical goals — which of the goals above (A–H) your innovation addresses
  5. Innovation strategy — which of the strategies above (1–4) best describes your approach
  6. Results or observations — what impact you have observed, even if informal or anecdotal
  7. (Optional) Link to resources — a link to a web page, platform, or material you use with your students that illustrates your approach

Submissions do not need to be polished academic papers. We value practical experience and honest reflection over formal research methodology. 

What happens next

The selection process will seek to ensure representation across different disciplines, so that the resulting compendium and workshop reflect the breadth of teaching contexts within the alliance.

Selected contributions will be:

  • Featured in a UNINOVIS compendium of innovative teaching practices shared across all partner institutions
  • Invited to make a presentation (10 minutes + 2 minutes for questions) of their proposal at UNINOVIS Virtual Workshop Innovative Teaching Practices in the Age of AI. Note that time constraints may force the organisers to limit the number of invitations.
  • Considered for participation in an in-person workshop during the spring of 2027

Committees

The scientific committee will evaluate proposals and select the ones that will go forward.

catalogue_events.name: Visual Intelligence: The European Business Intelligence Hackathon
catalogue_events.description: This hackathon introduces students to Decision Information Systems (BIS) and Business Intelligence (BI) tools for data-driven decision-making. Born from a collaborative reflection between European academic staff, it combines an online preparatory phase with an intensive face-to-face week in Paris. Students work in international groups to solve a real-life BI challenge by designing data warehouses and interactive dashboards.
catalogue_events.x_programme:
Preparatory Phase (February): Online video lectures and practical tutorials covering ETL, multidimensional modeling, Power BI/Power Query fundamentals, and DAX basics.

Intensive Phase (April 6-10): Hands-on experience at USPN. Students transform raw data using Power Query (M language), conceptualize dashboards, and integrate customized data visualizations from the community.
